profile.headline: Lead Software Engineer at State Farm
profile.summary:
Technical Skills:
 Programming languages: C, C++, Java, Groovy, SQL, PL/SQL, UNIX shell scripting, Perl, PHP
 Databases: Oracle, DB2, MySQL, Postgres, Perl DBI
 Operating systems: UNIX (AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris), Windows
 Network monitoring: IBM Tivoli Netcool suite (OMNIbus, Impact, ITNM, TNPM, TBSM, TCR)
 Protocols: SNMP, Syslog, TL1, SONET

positions.title: Network Operations Specialist III
positions.description:
Senior network monitoring and automation engineer responsible for fault and performance monitoring of Frontier’s switching, transport and data equipment as well as automating run book procedures to improve the operational efficiency of the NOC.

Built and supported monitoring solutions using IBM’s Tivoli Netcool suite (OMNIbus, Impact, ITNM, TNPM and TCR (Cognos)).

Designed and created NOC automation using Netcool Impact and Resolve (Groovy) to improve the efficiency of the NOC by automatically handling important tasks.

Created custom scripts for data collection and health monitoring of the monitoring applications using Perl, UNIX shell scripting and SQL.

Created and executed failover test plans on a periodic basis to ensure high availability of the monitoring applications for the 24x7 NOC.

Mentored less experienced team members on how to support and enhance the monitoring tools.

Skills: Tivoli Netcool, Resolve, Java, Groovy, Perl, shell scripting, SQL.

positions.title: Senior Network Management Operational Engineer
positions.description:
Senior operational engineer for a company developing a next generation broadband service delivery solution.  The NOC environment included the following Tivoli Netcool products: OMNIbus, Webtop, Impact, and ISMs. Several open source tools were also used, such as LooperNG, RTG, rsyslog and Net-SNMP.

Responsible for supporting all of the monitoring applications as well as troubleshooting and resolving operational issues.

Created and tested disaster recovery plans for NOC applications and tools.

Developed custom tools using UNIX shell scripts, Perl, Python, PHP and HTML.

Created and updated Netcool probe rules and Impact policies to support business logic.

Created NOC screens that show the health of the network and monitoring tools.

Skills: Tivoli Netcool, Java, Perl, Python, PHP, HTML, shell scripting.

positions.title: Sr. Infrastructure Engineer
positions.description:
Senior Tivoli Netcool administrator for a multi-client monitoring environment used to monitor network devices and servers for Capgemini’s customers. The environment included the following Tivoli Netcool products: OMNIbus, ITNM, Impact, TBSM, ITM and ITCAM ISMs.

Installed and configured ITM (IBM Tivoli Monitoring) agents for monitoring operating systems, log files, databases, Netcool OMNIbus ObjectServers and TBSM.

Designed and built new monitoring using Impact policies and TBSM service models.

Worked on Netcool OMNIbus integrations with Remedy ITSM and DB2 event archives.

Performed Netcool application upgrades and failover testing.

Trained onshore and offshore team members on Netcool application administration.

positions.title: Senior Systems Management Architect
positions.description:
System administrator and architect for a large Netcool event management system that monitored servers and network devices for clients. Responsible for designing system improvements and upgrades while maintaining high-availability.

System administrator and architect for a distributed server monitoring environment using Nimsoft’s NimBUS. Responsible for working with subject matter experts to define standardized metrics for server and application monitoring. Replaced customers’ monitoring tools, such as OpenView, NetIQ and MOM, with NimBUS.

Integrated new clients and new monitoring tools into the event management system.

Assisted with technical content in sales proposals for new event management projects.

Presented demonstrations of monitoring capabilities to potential customers.

positions.title: Managing Consultant
positions.description:
Designed and implemented network management and systems management solutions for IBM clients using Tivoli Netcool products. The Netcool solutions included the following Netcool products: OMNIbus, Webtop, SSMs, ISMs, TBSM and Impact.

Project Summary:
______________

AT&T (Austin, TX): Updated a Netcool deployment in a development lab to handle the next release of a business-grade VoIP solution. Developed procedures for migrating the solution to the production environment. Trained the Netcool administrators.

Atlanta Public Schools (Atlanta, GA): Customized an existing Netcool deployment to monitor four of the school district’s critical business applications. Trained the Netcool administrator and Tier 1/Tier 2 support personnel.

CenterPoint Energy (Houston, TX): Used Netcool products to create real-time dashboards for monitoring SAP business applications and an application for dispatching work orders to mobile technicians. 

Sprint Nextel (Reston, VA): Used Tivoli Netcool products to build a service quality management solution for a new “push-to-talk” phone service. Used Java and Perl to write custom integrations with the data sources.

SunTrust Banks (Atlanta, GA): Installed and customized a new fault monitoring solution for SunTrust’s network operations center. The Netcool solution was integrated with a trouble ticketing system and an event archive database for historical reporting.

positions.title: Consultant
positions.description:
Deployed and customized network management and systems management solutions for ReachView clients using Netcool products. The Netcool solutions included the following products: OMNIbus, Webtop, ISMs, SSMs, TSMs, Impact, Reporter and Proviso.

Project Summary:
_________________

Emdeon (Nashville, TN): Installed a performance management system to monitor network devices and servers. Built custom reports for displaying the performance data.

Globix (New York, NY): Integrated two separate fault management systems to support the 
merger of Globix and NEON Communications. The integration work involved combining probe rules, database schemas and automated procedures.

Hawaiian Telcom (Honolulu, HI): Installed and configured a fault management system for monitoring the Hawaiian Telcom telephone and data networks. Configured a performance management system to provide data trending analysis.

Insight Communications (Louisville, KY): Customized the web-based interface of a cable internet fault management system. Wrote probe rules for new devices and customized existing probe rules based on client feedback. 

Verio (Dallas, TX): Customized a fault management system for a global data network. Customized the web interface based on customer feedback. Installed and configured probes for monitoring Oracle and SAP applications.

positions.title: Analyst Programmer
positions.description: Used Netcool products to set up demo scenarios to support sales of next generation network solutions. The scenarios included fault management, performance management and service level agreement monitoring of cable, VoIP and wireless networks.

positions.title: Software Verification Contractor
positions.description:
Tested a Windows application that generates detailed sales quotes for telecom equipment.

Wrote test plans and individual test scripts.

Performed automated testing using WinRunner.

positions.title: Member of Technical Staff II (Software Engineer)
positions.description:
Designed and developed a real-time embedded fault detection and management system for a SONET ADM. Software was event driven and used inter-process communication.

Worked on low-level and high-level software layers. The low-level work included direct memory manipulation, handling interrupts and optimizing code. The high-level work included consolidating information from lower layers, interfacing with other subsystems and handling user requests.

Code was developed using C and ran on UNIX (Solaris) and OSE (a real-time embedded operating system) platforms. Code was stored under ClearCase version control.

Provided continuing engineering support. Made enhancements, investigated problem reports and fixed defects discovered internally and by customers.

Performed regression testing to ensure software stability during development phases.

positions.title: Member of Scientific Staff (Software Engineer)
positions.description:
Designed, developed, tested, documented and supported application software for wireless and wireline telephone switches within groups of about 5 to 10 engineers. The applications included performance monitoring, fault management, billing and in-service software upgrades.

Software design process included object-oriented methodologies such as class diagrams, use-case scenarios and message sequence diagrams.

Software was developed using C++ and ran on a PowerPC processor running UNIX (AIX).

Provided departmental software load build support for about 50 people (on-call 24/7). This         involved monitoring software builds, writing compilation and installation utilities using UNIX shell scripts and helping users with their local development environments.

Presented demos of applications to customers on-site and at user group meetings.
